outcome.technical: New tools/reach-diff.py: `python3 tools/reach-diff.py <module> <suite> --base <rev> --head <rev> [--repo PATH] [--jobs N] [--timeout S] [--tracer monitoring|settrace]`. Exit 0 when no line is lost, 1 when one is, 2 on a usage error or when no comparison could be made. It never writes the checkout. Each revision is a `git archive` export streamed through tarfile into a mkdtemp scratch, removed in `finally` through _suite.remove_tree. The suite runs through the sweep's own run_one and grade, loaded with _loader.load as prove-gates does, so children get the sweep's cwd, TMPDIR, HOME, git config and session-variable filtering. There is one job per STAGES block (`--selftest --stage LABEL`), or one whole-file run when sweep.is_staged or sweep.stage_labels say no. Both revisions' jobs share one ThreadPoolExecutor of sweep.default_jobs() workers; the default timeout is twice the sweep's DEFAULT_TIMEOUT. The tracer is a sitecustomize module written to a scratch directory that is put first on PYTHONPATH, so it runs in every Python process the suite starts, children included. It also runs the sitecustomize it shadows (Homebrew's). It keeps only lines whose code object's file resolves to the module: sys.monitoring LINE with DISABLE after the first event per location, or sys.settrace plus threading.settrace on the 3.8 floor (`--tracer settrace` forces it). Each process writes a JSON file at exit, renamed into place. Lines are matched by (enclosing dotted function from the AST, stripped text, occurrence index within that function), never by number. Lines reached at base whose key the head module no longer holds are listed apart as `gone` and do not decide the exit code. Any failed block (red case, crash, timeout, no contract line) or a revision that reached no line of the module refuses with 2. The docstring states what the tracer cannot see: -I/-E/-S children, an env without the hook, os._exit, kills, timeouts. Selftest: 16 cases on a scratch git fixture repo with one tag per variant (moved, reworded, drop-positive, drop-child, red-case, crash, untouched, plain-base/plain-drop) plus key and usage units. `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tools/reach-diff.py` exit 0, 16 cases. Also green under the sweep: tests/test__output_lints.py (173), tools/_suite.py (35), tests/test__refs.py (292), tests/test__deps.py, tests/test__areas.py, tests/test_derive_phase_gate.py (36), tools/gate-parity.py (119), tools/affected.py (57), tools/check-committed-pii.py (51); that run printed `8/8 files ok, 986 cases`, exit 0. `ruff check` exit 0; `vermin -t=3.8-` exit 0. CONTRIBUTING.md: one Hard-rules bullet after 'New behavior => new selftest cases' naming the tool as the check a conversion owes. It says, in its own sentence, that nothing runs the tool automatically: no verify.sh slice, no hook; it runs where a task names it in its gate. REAL RUN: `python3 tools/reach-diff.py plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py tests/test_drive_phase.py --base 92c399f5 --head HEAD`, exit 1, 716.9 s wall (user 1935.7 s, sys 1289.7 s), 8 jobs, measured once. Base 92c399f5: 5808 lines reached, 125 blocks, 6760 processes traced. Head c12794395e9b: 5784 lines, 77 blocks, 4846 processes. Lost: 35 lines in 13 functions, all quoted with line numbers in the report to the orchestrator. They include the advance sign-off route (triage 7564-7567 and 7569, drive_locked 9295-9299), drive_task's stop-blocked 9121-9124, apply_phase_answer's breach/no-ff/leave answers (8990, 8993, 8995, 8996), gate_went_red 7008-7013, close_task 4263 (review-answer) and rounds_cost_lines 7457-7460. Two lines the brief expected are NOT lost, and that was checked independently: drive-phase.py is byte-identical between 92c399f5 and HEAD (`git diff --stat` printed nothing), and a separate trace of HEAD's blocks alone (scratchpad/head_only.py, 485 s, no block failed, again 5784 lines) shows line 9313 `return drive_task(ctx, state)` and 9867 `lines.extend(ado_echo_lines(ctx))` reached at HEAD, while 7564, 7565, 9295 and 9296 are not. So the one-task route and the ADO echo were covered again before P152.2/P152.3 landed; the advance sign-off route is still a real gap at HEAD.
outcome.descriptive: A test conversion can now be checked mechanically: tools/reach-diff.py names every line of a module the old suite reached and the new one does not. Its first run over the drive suite found 35 such lines, including the advance sign-off route.

testsAdded: tools/reach-diff.py rd1-rd16 on a scratch git fixture. Dropping the only block that reaches a branch exits 1 naming exactly that line and function (rd1). A pure move exits 0 with no gap and nothing gone (rd2), over a fixture whose reached line numbers differ between revisions (rd3). Lines reached only in a child interpreter are measured (rd4). A red case, a crashed suite, and a revision reaching no line each exit 2 (rd5-rd7). A suite with no STAGES runs whole (rd8). The settrace fallback agrees (rd9). Line keys separate occurrences and survive a move (rd10, rd11). Usage errors exit 2 (rd12-rd14). The compared repository is never written (rd15). A reworded reached line is listed as gone and decides nothing (rd16).
